issue_context.title: Agnhost webhook being able to inject sidecar
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:
There is the Agnhost image used for e2e test purposes. It supports webhook that can mutate pods adding init container. It would be useful to have functionality for adding containers.

**Why is this needed**:
I'm planing to add e2e test for k8s vertical pod autoscaler. It requires sidecars.

review_comments: what does the pause container do when it gets a term signal? will adding it here make the pods with this injected sidecar wait for the default grace period when deleted, or does the pause container exit quickly?
unconditionally adding an init container is not idempotent (will fail if the webhook is rerun), so the existing code looks incorrect

> unconditionally adding an init container is not idempotent (will fail if the webhook is rerun), so the existing code looks incorrect

I'm not sure I understand... I'm removing pod name matching so it should be unrelated to webhook being rerun. Could you give me an example of a scenario?
Plus, patch that it's used overrides existing initContainers, so result should always be the same...

The existing code always appends a container to the pod being admitted. That is not idempotent (if the webhook is called twice while admitting the pod, it will append two identically named containers, which will fail validation). It should only append the container if the named injected container does not already exist.

Ok, I understand that I need to add this check for sidecar injection, so thanks for  point it out :)

But the adding initContainer should still work fine. The patch used for initContainers is `"{"op":"add","path":"/spec/initContainers","value":[{"image":"webhook-added-image","name":"webhook-added-init-container","resources":{}}]}"`, which should override the list.
Imho `{"op":"add","path":"/spec/initContainers/-","value":{"image":"webhook-added-image","name":"webhook-added-init-container","resources":{}}}` should add an init container to the existing list.

> But the adding initContainer should still work fine. The patch used for initContainers is "{"op":"add","path":"/spec/initContainers","value":[{"image":"webhook-added-image","name":"webhook-added-init-container","resources":{}}]}", which should override the list.

That is not well-behaved as a webhook... it means if a subsequent admission webhook appended an initContainer, then this webhook was called again, it would undo the other webhook's change. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/extensible-admission-controllers/#idempotence

`mutatePod' should have unchanged logic now. I also added check for the sidecar so the webhook should be idempotent.
PTAL
